title: Pueblo County Sheriff marks three years in office - NewsBreak
text:
By Brett Yager No media credit provided. ,
1 days ago
(PUEBLO COUNTY, Colo.) — Pueblo County Sheriff David J. Lucero marked three years as the 38th Sheriff, and emphasized the responsibility of the role and the people behind the work.
The Pueblo County Sheriff’s Office (PCSO) said that since Sheriff Lucero took office, the department has been focused on strengthening professional standards, improving public safety outcomes, and building long-term solutions that serve both employees and the community.
Pueblo County Sheriff David J Lucero, Courtesy: Pueblo County Sheriff’s Office “Serving Pueblo County as Sheriff has been the greatest honor of my career,” said Sheriff Lucero. “The progress we’ve made over the past three years is because of the men and women of this office, deputies, detention staff, communications professionals, and civilian employees, who show up every day committed to doing the job the right way, professionally, constitutionally, and with accountability.”
A cornerstone of the commitment is national accreditation. PCSO said under Sheriff Lucero’s leadership, the office earned a third “Triple Crown” recognition from the National Sheriffs’ Association, placing Pueblo County among a few agencies nationwide accredited simultaneously in law enforcement, corrections, and correctional health care.
Sheriff Lucero’s focus on professionalism has translated into measurable results, according to PCSO. In 2025, deputies responded to more calls for service, a 7.4% increase in total incidents, while overall criminal incidents fell by 4.8% compared to 2024.
Total arrests rose 55.8% and DUI arrests more than doubled, which PCSO said reflects a deliberate emphasis on proactive enforcement and on traffic safety. Motor vehicle theft declined during the same period.
“The Sheriff’s Office has also taken deliberate steps to support staffing stability, including pay structure improvements and incentive programs for critical positions, recognizing the nationwide challenges facing law enforcement recruitment and retention,” said PCSO.
Sheriff Lucero’s priority, looking forward, is detention operations, advancing the new Pueblo County detention facility, replacing the current downtown jail. The new detention facility will be a safer, more secure, and more efficient environment for staff, those in custody, and the public.
“As the Sheriff’s Office enters its next chapter, the mission remains unchanged: to deliver professional, accountable public safety services, invest in people and systems that work, and maintain transparency with the Pueblo County community.”
